title.narrative: Support to the Royal Commission for Makkah City and Holy Sites (RCMC)

description.narrative:
Makkah City is the birthplace of the Prophet Muhammad and is the location of the Grand Mosque (Masjid Al Haram) in which the Kaaba, a shrine that Muslims consider the most sacred spot in the world, is housed. Madinah City, a road distance of about 350 km to the north of Makkah City, provided the Prophet Muhammad with sanctuary when he fled Makkah, and is where he was instrumental in establishing the first mosque built in Islam, the Quba Mosque (Masjid Quba). The two holy sites attract millions of pilgrims every year.
In 2020, Makkah City, was home to an estimated 2 million people, representing an average annual growth rate of 2.6% since 2015, making it the third largest city in KSA. However, overall, since 1989, its population has grown by 150% while the Makkah urban area has increased by over 300% in the same period. At the same time, the number of pilgrims visiting Makkah for Hajj and Umrah has increased exponentially over the years, subjecting the city to a significant fluctuation of residents and associated logistical challenges . Other challenges, as highlighted by the Future Saudi Cities Programme, concern the high number of informal settlements. In Makkah, there are approximately 65 unplanned settlements spread across 16 primary locations and consisting of roughly 40% of the Holy City’s total population. They are characterized by lack of basic services and amenities, poor quality, and often unsafe, living conditions, and lack of public spaces and public services within easy reach .
To enable Makkah City and the adjacent Holy sites to serve 30 million visitors in terms of accommodation, public utilities, telecommunications, etc., the RCMC is developing and implementing a multifaceted, multidimensional approach that will result in adequate quality service provision for the target number of visitors and the improvement of the quality of life in Makkah across health, education, transportation and other sectors. To this end, the RCMC plans to work closely with the public, private and non-governmental stakeholders, as well as international development partners, to identify programs and projects that will help make Makkah one of the world’s most attractive cities.
The project aims to deliver a Detailed Master Plan and Urban Design for the City of Makkah to guide decision-making on planning and design, location, siting, control, implementation, management, administration, monitoring and follow up of future development within the entire City of Makkah and, to a lesser extent, the wider RCMC jurisdiction. It will include key areas, transit-oriented developments (TODs) and Mawaqit (religious entry zones for Hajj and Umrah). The DMP will be based on Vision 2030 and the Makkah Conceptual Master Plan's deliverables and will include megaprojects as well as projects with strategic importance that are under construction or in the pipeline.
